diagnostic_evidence.quote:
An operator $T:C(\Omega)\to C(\Omega)$ is called a \emph{positive $\varepsilon$-contraction} if for any $g\in C(\Omega)$,
\[
    \|g^{+}-Tg\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}
    \le (1-\varepsilon)\|g^{+}\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}.
\]

issues.failure_explanation: Definition 4.2 defines a positive $\varepsilon$-contraction solely through the norm bound $\|g^+ - Tg\|_{L^\infty} \le (1-\varepsilon)\|g^+\|_{L^\infty}$, which only implies $-(1-\varepsilon)\|g^+\|_{L^\infty} \le g^+(\bmx) - Tg(\bmx) \le (1-\varepsilon)\|g^+\|_{L^\infty}$. The proof of Lemma 4.4 asserts without justification that $0 \le g^+(\bmx) - Tg(\bmx)$ and $0 \le g^-(\bmx) - T(-g)(\bmx)$. Without the lower bound $Tg \le g^+$, $a(\bmx) - b(\bmx)$ can have magnitude up to $2(1-\varepsilon)\|g\|_{L^\infty}$, so $Sg$ is not guaranteed to be a balanced $\varepsilon$-contraction.

failure_location.quote:
Applying the positive $\varepsilon$-contraction property to $g$ and $-g$ gives, for all $\bmx\in\Omega$,
\[
    0\le g^{+}( mx)-Tg(\bmx)
    \le (1-\varepsilon)\|g^{+}\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\le (1-\varepsilon)\|g\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},
\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the condition $0 \le Tg \le g^+$ (condition (C1)) to the hypothesis of Lemma 4.4 or to Definition 4.2 of a positive $\varepsilon$-contraction.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 4.4 is false as stated for general positive $\varepsilon$-contractions that do not satisfy the pointwise domination $Tg \le g^+$.
issues.title: Omitted one-sided bound in definition or hypothesis for balanced contraction lemma
issues.why_classification: Adding the local condition $0 \le Tg \le g^+$, which is already established for operators satisfying condition (C1) in Lemma 4.3, is a routine repair that preserves the lemma and all downstream usages without new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Based on $\psi$, we define the $d$-dimensional function
\[
\Psi(\bmx)
\coloneqq
\frac{1}{d}\sum_{i=1}^d \psi(x_i).
\]
The cutoff function associated with $Q$ is then defined by the rescaled map
\[
\Gamma_Q(\bmx)
\coloneqq
\Psi\!\left(\tfrac{2}{\ell(Q)}\bigl(\bmx-\bmc(Q)\bigr)\right),
\]

A \emph{(continuous) cutoff function} associated with $Q$ is any map $\Gamma_Q : \R^d \to [0,1]$ satisfying
\[
\Gamma_Q(\bmx)=1 \ \text{for } \bmx\in Q,\quad
0\le \Gamma_Q(\bmx)\le 1 \ \text{for } \bmx\in rQ\setminus Q,\quad\tn{and}\quad 
\Gamma_Q(\bmx)=0 \ \text{for } \bmx\notin rQ.
\]

issues.failure_explanation: For $d \ge 2$, $\Psi(\bmx) = \frac{1}{d}\sum_{i=1}^d \psi(x_i)$ vanishes only when $\psi(x_i) = 0$ for all $i \in \{1,\dots,d\}$, i.e., when all coordinates satisfy $|x_i| \ge r$. Whenever even a single coordinate satisfies $|x_i| < r$, $\Psi(\bmx) \ge \frac{1}{d}\psi(x_i) > 0$. Thus $\Gamma_Q(\bmx)$ does not vanish outside $rQ$, but is strictly positive along infinite coordinate slabs. Consequently, the overlap sum $\sum_{i} \Gamma_{Q_{g,\eps,i}}(\bmx)$ cannot be bounded by $2^d$ using Lemma 4.6, (4.3) fails, and $T_\eps g(\bmx)$ does not vanish where $g^+(\bmx) = 0$. Hence condition (C1) fails, and $T_\eps$ is not a positive $\varepsilon$-contraction. Downstream, in Theorem 3.1, $h_k$ does not vanish on the set where $f < 0$, so subtracting $h_k$ strictly increases $|f_{k+1}|$ there, violating pointwise domination and strict $L^p$ residual decrease.

failure_location.quote:
If instead
\[
\bmx\notin \bigcup_{i=1}^{n_{g,\varepsilon}} rQ_{g,\varepsilon,i},
\]
then $\Gamma_{Q_{g,\varepsilon,i}}( mx)=0$ for all $i$, and hence
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:Tg:outside}
T_\varepsilon g(\bmx)=0 .
\end{equation}
Combining \eqref{eq:Tg:upper}, \eqref{eq:g:lower}, and \eqref{eq:Tg:outside}, we conclude that
\[
0 \le T_\varepsilon g(\bmx) \le g^+(\bmx)
\quad  \text{for all }\bmx\in[0,1]^d,
\]
which establishes condition~\ref{item:T:C1}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must construct true localized multidimensional cutoff functions that vanish outside $rQ$ (such as via products or depth-based intersection operations) and provide a multigrade architecture capable of computing them, which cannot be achieved with single-hidden-layer updates of width $5d$ for $d \ge 2$.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 4.7, Theorem 3.1, Theorem 1.1, and Corollary 1.2 are invalidated for all dimensions $d \ge 2$. The guaranteed uniform convergence and monotonic $L^p$ error decay of multigrade neural networks of fixed width $5d$ are left unsupported.
issues.title: Multidimensional cutoff definition is not compactly supported, invalidating positive contraction and grade-wise error decay
issues.why_classification: The failure invalidates the central theoretical guarantees of the paper (Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 3.1) in dimension $d \ge 2$. Resolving it requires a fundamentally different proof architecture and alterations to the neural network design to compute localized multivariate cutoffs.
